title: Operator Investigation Cookbook: lightweight telemetry recipes for token-serving incidents
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operator-focused cookbook of telemetry recipes for fast investigation of token-serving incidents (high tail latency, sudden cost spikes, cold cache regressions, multi-model fanout anomalies). It is intentionally pragmatic: small sets of signals, trace anchors, and dashboard widgets you can spin up quickly and rely on during paged incidents.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to hosted and dedicated inference paths. Private deployments may need local query tweaks.
- Assumes standard instrumentation: request id (x-request-id), tenant_id, model_name, route, host/pod, kv_cache_hit boolean, batch_size, queue_time_ms, decode_time_ms, total_tokens.
- Focus is on investigation signals (not metric hygiene or long-term SLI design).

Quick signal map (what to look at first, order matters):
1) Global intake: requests_per_minute, internal_error_rate(5m), 95th_total_latency_ms
2) Cold-cache indicator: prefix_cache_hit_rate (5m window), tenant_cold_cache_surge_count
3) Routing/backpressure: queue_time_ms(p50/p95), batching_ratio = tokens_generated / gpu_tokens_processed
4) Fanout & model variants: per-request model_fanout_count, model_variant_latency_p95
5) Cost-correlated: tokens_per_request and token_error_ratio (output truncation or streaming abort)
6) Traces: span-count-per-request, long-running spans (kernel_exec ms > 200), unexpected sync-block spans

Minimal metric definitions (operator-friendly):
- total_requests: counter, incremented at API ingress with labels [tenant_id, route, model_name, revision]
- successful_responses: counter, labels as above
- error_responses: counter, labels [tenant_id, route, model_name, status_code, error_class]
- total_token_emitted: counter, labels [tenant_id, model_name]
- kv_cache_hit: counter, labels [tenant_id, model_name, prefix_hash]
- request_queue_time_ms: histogram (buckets: 0,1,2,5,10,25,50,100,250,500,1000), labels [host, pool]
- kernel_exec_time_ms: histogram (buckets tuned to GPU/CPU profiles), labels [cuda_device, model_shard]
- span_count_per_request: gauge (observed per-completed request)
- model_fanout_count: histogram (1..8), label [request_id]
- batch_utilization_pct: gauge updated per-batch run, labels [pool, model_name]

Span design anchors (trace snippets we want on every request):
- Ingress span: tags {request_id, tenant_id, route, model, model_revision, client_version} and event "received"
- Router decision span: duration of routing policy eval (should be <1ms normally). Tag: decision={local, fallback, queue}, dest_pool
- KV cache check span: short async span; annotate with prefix_hash and hit=true/false. If miss, include approximate_prefix_len
- Batching span: includes batch_size, batch_id, batch_start_ts, batch_finish_ts, queue_time_ms aggregated
- Kernel exec span(s): include shard_id, cuda_device, token_start_index, token_end_index, peak_mem_gb, exec_ms. If exec_ms unusually high, require kernel logs ref
- Emit span: token_count_emitted, stream_aborted boolean

Trace sampling & prioritization recipe:
- Default: probability sampling 0.5% for low-cost capture across production and 100% for traces where any of: error_responses>0, request_queue_time_ms p95>100ms, kv_cache_hit==false and tokens>256, model_fanout_count>2
- Severity-weighted tail capture: when global p99 latency crosses configured threshold, escalate sampling of long-running spans to 100% for 30 minutes and notify on-call
- Privacy filter: strip prompt content from span attributes; persist prompt_token_count only

Three compact investigation dashboards (recipes you can create in <20m):
1) "Paging Triage" (single-row, single-screen):
   - Top: global request rate, error rate (1m/5m), p99 total latency
   - Middle: top 5 tenants by requests and by error rate (heatlist), prefix_cache_hit_rate by tenant
   - Bottom: live trace quick-links (recent traces with long kernel_exec_time) + top 3 hosts by queue_time_ms p95
   - Alert anchor: if p99 latency > SLA OR error_rate > 0.5% for 5m, link to runbook snippet
2) "Cold Cache Flash" (blast triage):
   - Compact timeseries: prefix_cache_hit_rate global and per-model (1m), eviction_rate per pool
   - Table: top 20 prefixes causing misses (prefix_hash, requests, avg_tokens, miss_rate) with quick action: prewarm candidate flag checkbox
   - Probe: synthetic probe success latency and kv_warm_flag (boolean)
3) "Capacity & Cost Heatmap" (ops view):
   - Heatmap: GPU utilization by pool x hour, color scaled by batch_utilization_pct
   - Scatter: tokens_per_request vs kernel_exec_time_ms per model (points colored by quantization_profile)
   - Cost-to-token: derived panel showing $/1M tokens by pool (approx from billing tags)

Investigation checklist (first 10 minutes):
- Step 0: capture incident context (time window, any recent deploys, rollout flags). Check rollout dashboard and PR deploy tags.
- 1: open Paging Triage dashboard; note tenants and hosts. Snapshot p95/p99.
- 2: run quick trace filter: request_queue_time_ms p95 > 100ms OR kernel_exec_time_ms > 200ms. Grab 3 traces.
- 3: check kv cache hit rate and top prefixes; if massive misses, trigger prewarm or short-circuit fallback model.
- 4: if fanout_count>1 present, inspect per-branch latency; identify slow variant.
- 5: if batch_utilization dropped < 30%, check autoscaler events and pool health (OOM, node drains).
- 6: escalate to infra on-call if kernel_exec_time correlates with single device (suspected noisy neighbor).

Quick queries (examples you can paste into metrics UI):
- Top hosts by queue p95: topk(5, quantile_over_time(0.95, request_queue_time_ms_bucket[5m]) by (host))
- Prefix misses last 5m: sum(rate(kv_cache_hit{hit="false"}[5m])) by (prefix_hash, model_name)
- Model variant p95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(kernel_exec_time_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, model_variant))

Dashboard widget UX notes (small things that help during incidents):
- Prefer tables with sortable columns and a small action column (link to trace, prewarm candidate).
- Use short-lived color annotations (e.g., transient red band) to mark the incident timeframe so reviewers know the focus window.
- Inline runbook snippets: the top-right of a triage dashboard should have a 2–3 step checklist with quick links (runbook, prewarm API, emergency-pool-toggle).

Runbook integration (how dashboards tie to playbooks):
- Create playbook sections keyed by the alert fingerprint (alerting rule id + impacted pool). Use the dashboard URL as the canonical triage view.
- Playbook quick actions: POST /ops/api/v1/pool-prewarm {pool_id, prefixes: []}, POST /ops/api/v1/route-fallback {route, target_variant}

Notes on async batch visibility:
- Batch boundaries are our single greatest blind spot. Emit batch_id with each request's trace and expose batch-level metrics (batch_size, queue_time_ms, batch_result_error_count).
- When investigating tail latency, collapse request-level traces to "batch parent" view to quickly see if a single batch created a domino effect.

Unresolved / open questions (decisions needed):
- What should the default prefix_cache_hit_rate sampling resolution be for high-traffic tenants? (tradeoff: cardinality vs actionable signal)
- How aggressive should synthetic prewarms be for large tenants? Any cost guardrails?
- Confirm label cardinality limits for prefix_hash in metrics storage (can we keep top-500 prefixes for 30d?)

Action items & owners (short):
- Marco: prototype the Paging Triage dashboard + inline checklist (due 2025-11-17)
- Daniel: add batch_id to trace root and emit batch-level histograms (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-prs/pull/92) (due 2025-12-01)
- Priya: run a retention/cost estimate for storing prefix_hash top-500 for 90 days (due 2025-12-08)

Notes to self / operator tips (small heuristics):
- If only one host shows kernel_exec spikes, suspect hardware or isolation issue — repro by routing a synthetic 512-token request to that host.
- Prefetching prewarm: start with a 30s TTL prewarm and tune based on miss half-life observed in the table.
- During paging, reduce dashboard refresh interval to 10s for critical panels and 60s elsewhere.

References and links:
- Runbook canonical: CONFLUENCE-1234
- Related tickets: JIRA-INF-847 (cold cache regression), JIRA-OPS-1190 (batch id traces)
- Telemetry PR: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-prs/pull/92

End - operator-investigation-cookbook: keep this doc short and practical. Update after next incident retro.
